Week 28 Appendix: A Week of Broad, Shallow Erosion

Across courts, campuses, and immigration, executive power widened while the clock barely moved, revealing damage measured in breadth, not depth.

This was a high-pressure week defined by executive aggrandizement, politicization of neutral institutions, and the use of immigration, trade, and information control as cross-cutting instruments of power. The strongest structural pressures came from efforts to bypass Congress on spending and tariffs, retaliatory or loyalty-based interventions in the judiciary, civil service, military promotions, and statistical agencies, and a broad campaign to discipline universities, media, and public narratives. Immigration enforcement remained a major site of democratic erosion: detention expansion, due-process bypasses, congressional access restrictions, and abusive detention conditions all reinforced a model of exceptionalized state power. At the same time, several court rulings and lawsuits showed democratic resistance—blocking birthright citizenship restrictions, preserving Planned Parenthood Medicaid funding, and challenging detention and tariff authorities—but these were mostly defensive checks against larger executive pushes. Overall, the week reveals a governing style that treats oversight, expertise, and procedural neutrality as obstacles to be overridden, while using selective transparency, patronage, and coercive administration to consolidate control.
